retraction.reason: Re-read on 24 September under A14(6) against the bar that replaced M44b’s: a record earns its place by carrying at least one honest edge to anything already in the atlas, and nothing is written in order to keep one. The corpus is 859 active events across all five lanes, not the Portuguese core M44b judged this against. Africa is in the atlas now, 139 active events, and the rising’s own article, at revision 1370627418, opens its § Causes with "After the Scramble for Africa among the major European powers in the 1880s, Germany reinforced its hold on several formal African colonies." That sentence names the scramble and not this rising, which is the chronology class this fire dropped nine A13 edges for, and scramble-for-africa is an umbrella, which batch 31a’s rule keeps off both ends of an edge. What it wants is to be filed under that umbrella — 1905 to 1907 is inside 1885 to 1914 — which is a filing and not an edge, and so not a reinstatement this pass may make.
